sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Certification and Security Auditing

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 26 November 2013, effective 1 January 2015)
France–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (effective 1967, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, applied provisionally)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50, including L.561-2-2 on UBO declaration; Décret n°2009-1087 du 3 septembre 2009; Loi n°2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II); Décret n°2016-1747 du 14 décembre 2016 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; AMF General Regulation for investment services ancillary to AEO supply-chain auditing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent government authority or notary in the country of origin (e.g., national identification bureau or registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) if the origin country is a party; otherwise consular legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified certificate of good standing of each corporate UBO (extrait de registre récent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent corporate registry in the entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and AML/CFT compliance declaration executed by the UBO's primary account-holding bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relevant regulated financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French consular legalization; signature legalization required where the bank is located in a non-Hague jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Financial Sanctions Vector, and France's national sanctions list under Article L.562-15 of the Code monétaire et financier; PEP checks must follow FATF 40 Recommendations and EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, requiring enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, senior public officials, and close associates; risk-based enhanced measures are triggered for entities incorporated in high-risk third countries identified by FATF or the EU delegated regulation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe – Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (access to the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés) and INPI – Registre National des Entreprises (RNE)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in French or another official EU language; any foreign-language corporate name must be transliterated into Latin characters, and the French mandatory suffix 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or its acronym 'SAS' must appear in the registration documents and on all official or commercial instruments.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, submit a written observation to the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce requesting reconsideration within 15 days of the notification; if the refusal is maintained, file an appeal before the chambre commerciale of the competent Tribunal de Commerce within one month of service of the rejection decision; alternatively, resubmit a modified name after conducting a fresh Infogreffe/RNE availability search and obtaining an official name clearance statement.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only where the domiciliation service is supplied by a licensed commercial agent or a Kbis-approved domiciliation company, and where the registered office has a physical reception facility in France able to receive judicial and administrative correspondence; for ISIC 7020 customs AEO supply-chain audit activities, a purely remote virtual address without any employee presence is insufficient to establish the real commercial substance required for customs pre-audit representations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% per annum for ordinary services companies; elevated cumulative likelihood of approximately 12–18% over the first three years where the entity files customs receipts and AEO-related audit reports with the French customs administration (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and UBO search fee at Infogreffe and RNE (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Infogreffe – Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI – Registre National des Entreprises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the tarif des greffes (schedule of court registrars) and prevailing market price per extract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and legalization/apostille of non-EU corporate documents (passport copies, certificate of good standing, bank references)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities (Hague Apostille office / French consulate in the jurisdiction of origin)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff (tarif consulaire) / statutory fee per document in the origin country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/PEP/OFAC/UN/French sanctions screening and UBO register filing via compliance attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Outside French avocat / compliance due-diligence service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per UBO file; flat fee for five persons

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of statuts (articles of association) by French avocat and incorporation representation before the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (avocat inscrit au barreau)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per engagement letter; statutory hourly rate no cap

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal formation notice in a French legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) and Kbis registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / e-Solen legal announcement platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for legal-announcement publication (regulated retail price) and registry fee tarif des greffes

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), arts. L.123-1, L.210-1 to L.210-10, L.227-1 to L.227-4 and R.227-1 to R.227-14; PACTE Law of 22 May 2019 and the 2023 company-formation reform implementing the INPI Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS); electronic filing through INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création de société / demande d'immatriculation d'une personne morale (successor to Form M0), lodged via the INPI Guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SAS; capital is freely fixed in the articles. For cash subscription, at least 50% of the nominal value of cash shares must be paid up upon incorporation, and the balance may be called within five years. Cash contributions must be deposited into a temporarily blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and are released only upon RCS registration. In-kind contributions are delivered immediately; a contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports) is required unless a statutory exemption is established, and is prudently retained where an in-kind asset exceeds EUR 30,000 or represents the main part of the capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF FR_SAS - adopted in writing by the sole shareholder on [date]. Resolved: 1. The share capital stated in the articles is subscribed in full by the shareholder; cash contributions are deposited in the blocked account until RCS registration. 2. The registered office is fixed at [French address], adopted as the statutory seat and official mailing address. 3. [Name] is appointed President and authorized daily manager; [AEO compliance officer] is appointed Head of Compliance for customs and AEO audit operations. 4. The President is instructed to publish notices, file the formation dossier, obtain the Kbis, and complete any incidental governance act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize and authenticate the SAS articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company counsel or qualified notaire where notarization is mandatory; eIDAS-qualified electronic signature service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Produce the final statuts in French containing corporate name, duration, statutory purpose (ISIC 7020 consultancy and AEO supply-chain security audit), registered office, share capital, governance provisions, powers of the President, and shareholder contributions. Use advanced electronic signature or, where real-estate or certain in-kind assets require authentication, execute before a notaire. Annex any draft report of the commissaire aux apports if the value of an in-kind contribution is material.
required_dossiers: Final signed articles of association in French
Draft President appointment and powers clause
List of subscribers with shareholding and contribution summary
In-kind contribution valuation report if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clause is challenged as unlawful, amend the relevant article by a written decision of the shareholder, re-sign the corrected articles, and upload the revised version through the Guichet unique without duplicating the original file unless the registry requires a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit paid-up share capital and obtain blocked-funds certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the proposed SAS or its subscribers, transfer the cash contribution, and request a blocked-funds attestation ('attestation de blocage des fonds'). The bank freezes the funds until the company produces the Kbis or a confirmed refusal of registration. Request the RIB to transfer the funds to the company account immediately after Kbis issuance.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of each subscriber
Proposed corporate details of the SAS
FATCA/AML and beneficial-owner questionnaire
Proof of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to AML/KYC concerns, submit notarized identity documents, source-of-funds records, and the complete beneficial-owner chain; if refusal persists, obtain a release order or choose another French credit institution and request a fresh blocking certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Place the mandatory legal publication notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal habilité à recevoir les annonces légales in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and submit the legal announcement stating the corporate form (SAS), corporate name, registered office, purpose, share capital amount and composition, duration, and identity of the President. Pay the insertion fee and obtain the justificatif de publication, which is mandatory for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Completed legal announcement form
Extract of the draft articles
Payment receipt for the insertion fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal requests correction, amend the omitted or incorrect particulars and republish; attach both the original and corrected publication certificates to the formation dossier to avoid a registry query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation dossier through the INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises - formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in and create the entity file; select 'création d'une personne morale' and populate all corporate data, governance appointments, registered office, and beneficial-owner declarations. Attach the certified PDF of articles, bank blocking certificate, legal publication certificate, appointment consents, identity documents, and the sworn non-conviction declaration of the President. Submit the file and pay the state registration fee online.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Bank blocked-funds attestation
Justificatif de publication in an approved legal gazette
Identity documents of the President and directors
Declaration of non-conviction and acceptance of office of the President
Beneficial-owner declaration
Report of commissaire aux apports if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries the dossier, respond within the rectification window by uploading the exact missing document or corrected statutory wording through the Guichet unique; do not open a new file unless the registry has deleted the original submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RCS registration and Kbis extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (RCS) via INPI Guichet unique and Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After verification, the registrar records the company at the RCS, issues the Kbis extract, and ensures the automatic generation of SIREN, SIRET and APE code (for ISIC 7020, APE 7022Z). Download the first Kbis from Infogreffe; it serves as conclusive evidence of legal existence for banking, lease, customs AEO audit, and contractual purposes.
required_dossiers: Receipt of online fee payment
Copy of the submitted formation dossier
Formation case reference issued by the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis issuance is delayed or contains errors, file a corrective request at Infogreffe or via the INPI Guichet unique with supporting registration evidence; the registry will issue a rectified Kbis within a short delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize tax, VAT, and employer registration synchronization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP Service des impôts des entreprises; URSSAF for employees; INSEE through registry transmission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that DGFiP automatically recognizes the company for corporate income tax and VAT based on the RCS data. If the VAT identification number is not assigned, write to the local SIE. If a physical office will be occupied, keep the lease and occupational risk assessment; if staff are hired, finalize URSSAF employer registration via net-entreprises.fr within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Articles of association
Registered office lease or accommodation certificate
VAT registration application or automatic assignment notice
URSSAF employer registration file if staff are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not received within 30 days, file a formal request with the local SIE attaching the Kbis and articles to obtain the intra-community VAT number. For URSSAF, a missing employer code should be escalated through the public business portal with proof of establishment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541614 is an office-based professional consulting and auditing business; no manufacturing or industrial establishment under the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) regime is created.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - AEO security audits are not a licensed profession in France. The company must provide services in compliance with the Union Customs Code and applicable data-security rules, but no state industrial operating permit is necessary.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable - no EIA authority because no installation or development requiring environmental assessment is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no registration, assessment, or authorization is required for administrative office operations under the Environmental Code provisions on classified installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or hazardous VOC/air emissions are generated. Office waste must be sorted and disposed under municipal waste rules; electrical and electronic waste must be remitted to certified take-back channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must maintain a fire-safety attestation for the applicable premises category if open to clients, and an up-to-date occupational risk assessment (document unique d'évaluation des risques - DUERP) under the Labour Code. No separate structural load inspection is required for ordinary administrative use; any structural certificate is a landlord obligation under applicable urban planning regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration and SIREN/TAX ID issuance coordinated through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, incorporation with the Guichet Unique automatically generates a SIREN number and, upon verification of economic activity, the intra-community VAT identification number (n° d'identification TVA intracommunautaire) with format FRXXYYYYYYYZZ (two-digit key + SIREN) issued by the DGFiP. A foreign entity without French incorporation but liable for French VAT (e.g., importing goods, holding stock, or supplying taxable services subject to French place-of-supply rules) must file a pre-registration questionnaire (form No. 2172-SD equivalent) with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) covering local establishment or direct VAT registration, and may be required to appoint an accredited tax representative (représentant fiscal) if not established in the EU; processing typically takes 2–4 weeks and requires proof of identity, articles of association, and evidence of the first taxable transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists under French law; an SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, article 206 CGI). Available elections include: (i) option for a single VAT taxable person / VAT grouping under article 256 C III CGI for related entities; (ii) option to waive the small-business VAT exemption (article 293 B CGI) to voluntarily become a VAT payer; (iii) option for the reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% for taxable profits up to €42,500 per tax year under article 219 CGI; (iv) election under the parent-subsidiary regime (régime mères-filles); and (v) hybrid mismatch counter-rules under articles 209 B, 209 C and 212 bis CGI (ATAD 2 transposition) restrict but do not create elective deductions — no check-the-box equivalent exists for entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies no general monetary registration threshold for taxable persons established in France; French-resident businesses must register from their first taxable euro, subject to the small-business exemption (franchise en base de TVA, article 293 B CGI) below €37,500 annual turnover for services and €85,000 for trade in goods (reduced ceilings of €34,600 and €81,500 with incremental tolerance). For non-French/EU suppliers providing digital services or intra-EU distance sales of goods, the €10,000 annual EU-wide threshold applies before French VAT registration is triggered. Foreign suppliers with no EU establishment are liable to register for French VAT on the first euro of taxable French supplies unless exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is phased in under the French e-invoicing reform: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive structured e-invoices and all large and mid-size enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 all small enterprises must issue structured e-invoices. Invoices must be transmitted through an accredited Dematerialization Partner Platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire — PDP) or the public portal Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), which forwards structured transaction data (including VAT summary and payment data) to DGFiP. This is a transmission/clearance model (not an Italian-style real-time fiscal stamping) but the formats must conform to EN 16931 (Factur-X, UBL, CII), and e-reporting of domestic B2C cross-border transaction data is transmitted to DGFiP near-real-time via the PPF. From 2026, non-compliant invoicing can trigger penalties of €15 per invoice up to €50,000 per entity per year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération à l'exportation) applies to the sale and physical dispatch of movable goods from France to a destination outside the EU provided proof of export is obtained within the statutory documentation window under articles 262-I-1° CGI. Services directly linked to exported goods (transport, handling, inspection) may also be zero-rated under article 262-I-2° CGI. Pure supply-chain audit consulting services (ISIC 7020) sold B2B to a non-EU customer are not technically zero-rated as exports: the place of supply is the recipient's country of establishment under article 259-1 CGI, rendering the French supply out of scope of French VAT (no VAT, no refund). If the same service is sold to a French VAT-registered client, domestic 20% VAT applies; if sold to an EU client, the reverse charge place-of-supply rule under article 259-1 CGI applies. To benefit from zero-rating on goods, the exporter must retain documentary proof of physical departure from the EU within 90 days of the invoice date (administratively accepted, not a strict statutory deadline) and obtain customs clearance validation through the DELTA export system.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/EXA) lodged electronically via the DELTA/Système de dédouanement, including the Export MRN (Movement Reference Number) and customs release certificate
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill or CMR/road consignment note evidencing physical departure from the EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/MT103 proof of settlement from the foreign buyer
Commercial Invoice (original) matching the customs declaration value and description
Proof of VAT registration status of the customer for B2B services (when applying reverse charge or non-EU out-of-scope treatment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration may retrospectively claw back zero-rated VAT (recouvrement de la TVA exonérée) if the export proof is missing, incomplete, or fraudulent, with the right of recovery extended to 10 years under article L.176 of the Livre des procédures fiscales where the absence of proof, bad faith, or fraudulent maneuvers is established (standard 3-year right for good-faith taxpayers). Penalties escalate under article 1729 CGI: 40% of the VAT in issue for deliberate non-disclosure (mauvaise foi), 80% for fraud with organized maneuvers (manœuvres frauduleuses); late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month under article 1727 CGI. Criminal tax fraud under article 1741 CGI carries fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, with additional customs penalties under the Code des douanes for false export declarations including confiscation of goods and fines equal to up to one time the value of the goods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) acting under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Regulations (Code monétaire et financier), in coordination with the European Central Bank for euro-area monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the euro area and the European Economic and Monetary Union; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no material restrictions on profit remittances or dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders, provided the source funds are legally repatriated earnings, corporate formalities (e.g., shareholder approval, tax clearance, and beneficial ownership documentation) are satisfied, and anti-money-laundering / know-your-customer verification is completed. For transactions with non-EU jurisdictions, EU capital movement provisions and French financial sanctions screening apply, but no general pre-approval is required except for specific regulated sectors or countries subject to EU restrictive measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds into euros. Exporters and entities performing cross-border services are free to retain foreign currency receipts in designated bank accounts; however, all cross-border payments above €10,000 must be reported to the French Customs and Indirect Taxation Administration (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects, DGDDI) or the Banque de France under the monthly balance-of-payments reporting regime (reporting circuit via a resident intermediary bank). The applicable statutory timeline is T+1 business day for reporting over the counter / postal transactions and T+5 business days for declaration amendments; the reporting threshold is €10,000 per transaction. No conversion ratio is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
La Banque Postale (via La Banque Postale Corporate & Treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for inbound EUR receipt and outbound EUR disbursement, and Low for serving as the sole treasury rail for a French SAS that needs to evidence statutory statutory capital deposits, given French bank account verification requirements for corporate registration. Offshore digital EMI institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business) are legally viable as add-on payment rails for settlement, provided (i) they hold an EU/EEA e-money institution license passported into France or an equivalent license recognized under the second Electronic Money Directive (2009/110/EC), (ii) they comply with the French AMF/FEA framework and register with the ACPR, and (iii) the SAS maintains a primary euro account with a prudentially supervised French credit institution. An offshore EMI not authorized in France cannot be used as the exclusive banking infrastructure for operational clearing or for satisfying the statutory deposit of share capital before incorporation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks generally require physical presence for corporate onboarding of a newly incorporated SAS, particularly for the legal representatives (President and, if applicable, General Director) and the beneficial owners. Physical presence is typically mandatory during the initial account opening interview at the bank branch or at a notary office. Remote onboarding is permitted on a limited basis for existing clients or for specific 'open-banking' digital account solutions offered by tier-1 banks, but documentary verification must be performed by a recognized third party, and a subsequent in-person or video-identification session (with qualified electronic signature via eIDAS) is almost always required. Non-resident directors must either appear physically at a French branch or complete an identity verification with a French consulate / apostilled notarized passport package. In practice, for a brand-new SAS with non-resident shareholders, physical appearance by the President or a duly authorized signatory is mandatory before the account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners with tax residency in high-risk third countries or complex multi-layer holding structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate structural chart with vehicle-by-vehicle ownership, certified copies of passports (apostilled), proof of address (utility bill < 3 months old), OECD tax residency certificates / RI (Résidence Fiscale) certificates for each beneficial owner, full identification of the ultimate natural person(s), audited financial statements of intermediate holding entities, and a written explanation of the source of funds to be injected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory capital deposit made via third-party payment or from a foreign jurisdiction with sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement showing the origin of the remittance, SWIFT MT103 with full sender/beneficiary details, commercial contract / deed of contribution (acte de constitution), notarized/shareholder resolution authorizing the capital contribution, proof that the sending entity is not on EU/OFAC/FATF sanctions lists, and a sworn AML source-of-funds declaration provided to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supposed AEO/supply-chain audit activity deemed as a consultancy service with potential 'perceived' tax evasion risk (e.g., recurring inbound payments from export customers with no clear underlying contract)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client engagement framework agreements, detailed invoices (factures) with reference to the AEO audit methodology and scope, delivery reports (pre-audit plan, on-site security verification checklist, post-audit remediation memo), evidence of professional indemnity insurance, and a forward-looking cash-flow forecast for at least 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or unverified inbound payments from unrelated parties exceeding €10,000 per transaction or €50,000 monthly cumulative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service agreements with pricing schedules, customer due diligence files (including KYB data and ultimate beneficial ownership), bank transfer purpose codes / SEPA payment reason codes, proof of performance (electronic audit logs, customs-related attestations), and, if applicable, an external auditor's / forensic accountant's verification of transaction trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS), the initial shareholder capital injection must be routed as a compliant international wire transfer to a French bank account opened in the name of the 'société en formation'. The wire must include a clear remittance info / purpose code: 'Capital Subscription – Incorporation of SAS' (French: 'Apport en capital social – Constitution de SAS'). The sending bank must use SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT if within SEPA zone) and the beneficiary must be the company account with the pre-registered RIB. French banks require the deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued by the receiving bank (Caisse des Dépôts or any French credit institution) for the notary / registration. For euro-area transfers, the purpose code shall be 'REMU' or 'SUBS' with settlement method 'CRED' and reference 'A000'. For transfers from third countries, the transfer must be accompanied by the underlying shareholders' resolution, certified ID passports of contributing shareholders, and a completed 'MTC' (Moyen de Télécompensation) declaration if the amount exceeds €10,000. The capital remains blocked on an escrow-like account (compte de dépôt) until legal incorporation is completed and the RCS registration is filed; upon issuance of the RCS receipt, the funds are converted to an operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade-related disbursements (payments to suppliers, contractors, logistics providers, and subcontractors in the AEO supply-chain audit business), the primary clearing rails are (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for euro-denominated payments within the EEA, governed by SEPA Regulation (EU) No 260/2012, and (ii) SWIFT MT103 (Customer Credit Transfer) for non-EEA or non-euro disbursements. Where the underlying transaction is a B2B trade settlement for goods or services, a Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit under UCP 600) may be used with the French bank as issuing or confirming bank, but for a service-oriented AEO audit (ISIC 7020) wire transfers are standard; no documentary credit is statutory mandatory. All outbound payments require a valid purpose code: for services, use 'SERV' (services) or the harmonized French reporting code 'SF' for balance-of-payments data; for contracts exceeding €100,000, supporting contracts and invoices must be retained for five years. Clearance timelines: SEPA CT within D+1 bank business day (or same-day if fast type), SWIFT MT103 normally 1-3 banking days depending on intermediary banks; AEO audit entities may request urgent processing by subscribing to 'Express Wire' / 'Urgent Transfer' services.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX Forward contracts (plain vanilla, with physical settlement)
EUR/other G10 and selected emerging-market currency Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) where the underlying currency is non-convertible or subject to limited settlement
Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs USD/GBP/CHF) for principal and interest exchanges under the ISDA Master Agreement
Currency options (European style) purchased over-the-counter from French credit institutions or licensed EU investment firms
FX spot contracts for operational conversions without speculative intent
Combination collar / zero-cost structures, limited to hedging genuine commercial exposure arising from invoiced consulting fees, customs audit project revenues, or international supplier payments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts with RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 1,500 EUR, potential company dissolution if not remedied within 3 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 2 months after year-end or 45 days after approval of accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% per month of unpaid tax, up to 80% of tax due, possible criminal sanctions
Fines and interest for late filing or payment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR or total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Accounting Plan (PCG) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual update of beneficial ownership information in corporate filings; no separate UBO register but declarations required upon changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard rate of impôt sur les sociétés applicable since 1 January 2022 to all French-resident companies)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit per fiscal year for SMEs satisfying CGI art. 219 conditions (annual turnover below EUR 10,000,000, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% held by individuals or qualifying companies). No R&D or zone-specific holiday applies to AEO audit activities; the Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure (capped at EUR 100,000,000 of qualifying costs per year) may in principle be claimed if the SAS performs qualifying consultancy-linked R&D. Net operating losses (déficits) may be carried forward indefinitely under art. 209 CGI, but the annual deduction is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income in excess of EUR 1,000,000; alternatively, a one-year carryback of up to EUR 1,000,000 of loss may create an immediate tax receivable.
